intro: Conditions without si. Almost all of these connectors take the subjunctive.
p.por si.nota: Por si takes the indicative: por si llueve.
p.como.nota: Como plus subjunctive: como llegues tarde, me voy.
b1.texto:
These take the **subjunctive**: the present for an open condition, the past for an imagined one.

- only if: **siempre que**, **siempre y cuando**, **con tal de que**, **a condición de que**. Te lo presto **siempre que** me lo **devuelvas**.
- unless: **a no ser que**, **a menos que**, **salvo que**. Iré, **a no ser que llueva**.
- in the event that: **en caso de que**. **En caso de que haya** problemas, llámame.
- a warning: **como**. **Como** no **estudies**, suspenderás.

Two keep the **indicative**: **por si** (llévate el paraguas **por si llueve**) and **salvo si** / **excepto si**, which behave like si.

Watch the mood: **siempre que** + indicative means whenever (siempre que **voy**, llueve), and **como** + indicative gives a cause (como **llegas** tarde, me voy).
b3.f0: Will you lend me your car on Saturday?
b3.f1: Yes, provided you give it back to me on Sunday.
b3.f2: Of course, unless there's a lot of traffic.
b3.f3: In case you have any problem, call me.
b3.f4: I'll take the charger in case I run out of battery.
b3.f5: And if you bring it back with no petrol, I won't lend it to you again.
b5.pregunta: Complete: I'll go, unless it rains.
b5.o0.refuerzo: A no ser que takes the subjunctive.
b5.o1.refuerzo: After a no ser que, the subjunctive.
b5.o2.refuerzo: The future cannot follow a no ser que.
b6.pregunta: Complete: take an umbrella in case it rains.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Por si is the exception: indicative.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Por si needs a conjugated verb.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I'll lend it to you provided you look after it.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Con tal de que takes the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: After con tal de que, the subjunctive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: With que you need a conjugated verb.
b8.pregunta: «Como llegues tarde, me voy.» What is como doing?
b8.o0.refuerzo: Como plus subjunctive is a condition.
b8.o1.refuerzo: That would be como llegas tarde, with the indicative.
b9.pregunta: «Siempre que voy, llueve.» With the indicative, siempre que means…
b9.o0.refuerzo: A habit: every time I go.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That is a no ser que.
b10.traduccion: In case you have any problem, call me.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write the conditions of an agreement between flatmates or business partners, using siempre que, a no ser que, con tal de que, en caso de que.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Negotiate aloud lending your car or your flat to a friend, setting your conditions.
